newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Daewoo Corp buys Bulgaria's only Sheraton.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo Corp buys Bulgaria's only Sheraton.

text.p: Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said on Monday it has sold a 67-percent stake in the Sheraton Sofia Hotel Balkan to South Korea's giant Daewoo Corp for $22.3 million.

Under the deal, approved by the cabinet on September 3, Daewoo has to invest some $5 million in Bulgaria's most luxurious hotel over the next five years. The amount of $22.3 million is due to be paid in cash.

Fifteen percent of the hotel will be offered for voucher privatisation and a further 17 percent will be offered to employees as preferential non-voting shares. One percent will be set aside as a reserve.
Bulgaria's only Sheraton hotel, favoured by foreign businessmen, has 154 rooms, 34 apartments, four restaurants and 504 employees. Its turnover in 1995 was 711 million levs ($3 million).

The International Monetary Fund has urged Bulgaria to speed up privatisation which so far has been slow. At the beginning of September it postponed crucial funding to the country until the government closes debt-ridden state firms or sells them.

The socialist cabinet of Prime Minister Zhan Videnov, in a bid to gain desperately needed IMF funding, approved on Sunday at a closed door session a final list of big state-owned companies that it plans to privatisate by the end of the year. The companies have not yet been announced.
-- Galina Sabeva, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561 ($ = 233.4 Bulgarian Levs)
